transcript.text: lg w/d keeps saying dE n wont start?? door is shut

The 'dE' code on LG washer-dryers means the machine thinks the door is not locked or closed properly. This is often caused by a small item of clothing getting caught in the rubber seal, preventing the latch from engaging fully. Please open the door and check the edges for any trapped fabric. Close it firmly until you hear a click, then try starting a cycle again. If it still shows dE, let me know.
ok checked, theres a duvet bulging against the glass n a corner squashed in the seal. shuts but springs back a bit

[Heading: Duvet blocking door latch]
That bulging duvet is almost certainly the cause of the 'dE' error. The machine needs the door latch to snap fully into place to lock it safely; if the fabric is trapped or pushing against the glass, the latch can't engage, so the machine refuses to start. If it starts, just reduce the load size next time (a single large item like a duvet often causes balance issues too).
ok so what do i do, take the duvet out? its mums n i need it washed before visitors come

[Heading: Obstruction preventing door lock]
Yes, you must take the duvet out to fix this. Open the door fully, pull the trapped fabric clear of the rubber seal and ensure nothing is caught in the latch mechanism. Close the door firmly until you hear a click, then try starting a cycle again. If it still shows 'dE' after clearing everything, the door lock itself may be faulty and would need an engineer to replace.
but how do i wash it then?? its a king size, does it need a smaller load or something? idk what the limit is

[Heading: Unbalanced load (single bulky item)]
To wash a king-size duvet safely in a washer-dryer, you must balance the weight. A single heavy item like a duvet will soak up water and stick to one side of the drum, causing an unbalanced load that stops the spin or triggers errors. 1. Add 2–3 large bath towels to the wash with the duvet. This helps distribute the weight evenly around the drum.
2. Select a programme specifically designed for 'Bulky Items', 'Duvet', or 'Bedding' if your model has one. These cycles use slower, gentler spins and more pauses to redistribute the load.
3. If no specific cycle exists, choose a standard Cottons cycle at 40°C with a low spin speed (e.g., 600–800 rpm). High spin speeds on a single heavy item are very likely to cause imbalance. Do not overload the machine; if it feels too tight when you push the duvet in, do not force it. If the machine still struggles or stops mid-cycle due to balance, stop it, redistribute the items by hand, and try again.
